name: Cefuroxime
summary: Second-generation cephalosporin (oral + IV) with improved coverage of H. influenzae and Moraxella; common for respiratory tract infections.
mechanism: Beta-lactam inhibition of penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs) blocks cell-wall synthesis; broader Gram-negative activity than first-generation agents.

dosing.adult: Oral: 250-500 mg PO every 12 hours; IV: 750 mg-1.5 g every 8 hours
dosing.renalAdjustment: Reduce dose/frequency in significant renal impairment

warnings: No Pseudomonas, MRSA, or reliable anaerobic coverage

clinicalPearls: Take oral cefuroxime axetil with food — absorption is significantly better
Covers H. influenzae and Moraxella catarrhalis — a step up from first-generation agents for respiratory use
good: Oral/IV second-generation cephalosporin well suited to respiratory tract infections.
bad: Not for Pseudomonas, MRSA, or meningitis; oral form has variable absorption.
